family_description: docs/ — the design and operations reference: what the system is, why it is that way, and how to run it. Drifts when the code changes underneath it, which is a different rate and a different repair from the agent-contract surfaces or the shipped SDK READMEs. Hence its own marker: a shared one would force the narrowest pass to lie about the widest surface.

anchor.why: The commit this pass was measured against. It is the marker's reason to exist: the next pass scans anchor..now instead of re-reading all history (expensive, so it gets skipped) or under-doing the tail (silent, so it gets trusted).

written by M27 (forecast honesty gates): the evidence floor, the flat band, the burn-rate corroboration, the zero-fill definition seam, and what refused[] means. docs/ALERTS.md ~94 referenced this file before it existed; that reference now resolves.

"Cost model" rewritten and an "Admission" section added by M5/D18, against crates/api/src/relay_result.rs and relay.rs. The flat $1 premise is gone: a run is priced envelope -> price book -> flat, and metadata.cost_source says which. Enqueue now evaluates the project's limits (429 on an enforcing breach, `warning` on the soft tier) while the settle-time event stays un-admitted. The stale $1 references elsewhere in the file (the diagram, the window-capacity note, the phase-2 changelog line) were repaired in the same pass; the rest of the document was read but not otherwise re-verified against the code.

D18 appended by M5 (relay runs are metered traffic; enqueue is the admission point), and D17's closing paragraph amended to point at it rather than assert the flat rate it deferred. No other decision was re-read against the code in this pass.

rewritten against crates/api/src/alerts/* for M3 (the persisted alert ledger). The two claims it used to make that the code no longer supports are gone: dedup is durable (Store::insert_alert_dedup, one atomic step per backend) rather than an in-memory map that resets on restart and lets each replica alert independently, and per-project routing exists rather than being deferred. Adds the eight alert kinds, the GET /v1/alerts surface, the X-LightTrack-Signature contract (including the sha256(secret) derived-key rule a receiver must implement), and the destination rules.

§6 updated by M22 (the contribution ledger): 'what left the building' moves from a preview to a record. Adds the collective_contributions table and its `contributions` Store surface, POST /v1/collective/contribute (the push now happens in the API and appends a row per attempt), GET /v1/collective/contributions, the unchanged-digest hash gate (generated_at excluded, so a no-op push makes no HTTP call and cannot trip a hub's min_interval), the hub_key_ref-by-name rule, JobKind::Contribute + the opt-in auto-contribute schedule, and DELETE ?all=1, which walks the ledger's hubs and reports the ones it cannot resolve to a URL. The rest of the file was NOT re-read against the code in this pass — only §6 is covered.

baseline_note: First marker for this family — 2026-08-24, written by the wave-2b registry-conformance drain. This was NOT a full pass. It rewrote one document (ARCHITECTURE §12, for the disk/retention/maintenance work landed the same day) and created two (the soak lane's contract and criteria), and it read §5/§11 of ARCHITECTURE while doing so. Everything else in docs/ is listed above as `not-in-this-pass`: unread against the code, not judged, not claimed. The three frozen archives are a separate category and stay out of scope permanently. The next pass's scope is therefore anchor..now PLUS the whole `not-in-this-pass` list — which is large, and saying so is the point: unbounded repair debt is not the drift itself, it is not knowing how much drift there is. What the pass incorporated: retention is now a stated, dated operator decision (unbounded, 2026-08-24) rather than an unexamined default, and the store has disk accounting, self-instrumentation and a lossless maintenance pass that ARCHITECTURE §12 describes. 2026-08-24, dated note on the mechanisms around this marker: crates/core/tests/catchup_marker_guard.rs now fails the build when a file under docs/ appears in neither list, and scripts/docs-catchup.sh computes this family's range and refuses loudly on a missing or unparseable marker. That those mechanisms exist is a fact; whether they hold is their own liveness evidence to produce, and no claim about it belongs here.
